F1.analysis: Independently traced DisplayConfigService.refresh -> BleManager.readDisplayConfig -> DisplayLease/exchangeDisplay -> transport notify parser -> FX commit. Background read holds commandTransactionLock for the batch, waits boundedly for legacyWaiters, validates connection generation and transport, and releases the lease before invoking the CP1 idle callback outside the transaction monitor. Existing typed identity, sleep, side-switch, ordinary-key, mode and runtime snapshot paths use the same transaction monitor. Mode switching increments the read ticket and prevents stale results from committing; mode completion triggers a current-mode refresh. The inspected controlled-order tests and logs support these paths, but do not constitute full Controller or hardware verification.

F2.analysis: The actual UI disables CP1 selection while display work, reads, or mode-change acknowledgement is pending. The service rejects conflicting display transactions before changing the preference; on an admitted device connection it persists the new mode only after a successful 0x98 acknowledgement and a still-current connection generation. A negative or uncertain response leaves the previous preference in force. Offline preference behavior remains local. This review found no premature UI success or write-around in the inspected call chain.

F3.analysis: Device-originated FX commits pass through operation and connection-generation checks and recheck live connection state. Per-field edit revisions prevent an ACK for an earlier value from clearing a newer same-value edit; preview duration begins at ACK time. Failure paths retain the local asset/configuration while marking device facts unconfirmed, and stale device callbacks do not overwrite the new connection state. The controlled FX tests cover their stated six stale-result combinations and same-value edit case; this is not an operating-system scheduling proof.

R1.analysis: Disconnect/session reset clears deferred SINGLE runtime state under commandLock. MULTI snapshots retain the generation at capture and verify it at the actual send entry/exit; stale pending state is not replayed by a new connection's idle callback. Existing current-connection preference application remains present. No mutation to slot-binding or TTL semantics was found in the reviewed diff. Physical reconnect lifecycle remains unverified.

per_file.analysis: Traced service wiring, shutdown, mode/sync guards, removal of legacy OLED/raw upload UI, target freezing before upload/clear, exact firmware-confirmation entry, and connection-change invalidation. Existing keyboard mode selection and old mode/light saves are gated around CP2 work; no bypass found.

Reviewed mutable FX state, resource map, brightness/effect dirty revisions, same-value edit protection, and ACK-timed 10-second preview state. State mutations are designed for FX-thread commits; no device IO is embedded.
Unknown codes have a nullable lookup distinct from legacy OFF fallback; UI save path can retain unknown values instead of silently writing OFF. Existing IDs/codes are unchanged in cumulative diff.

Reviewed CP2 opcodes, argument bounds, 19-entry capacity mapping, little-endian resource begin/chunk encoding, and CRC/frame sizing. No old protocol constants were removed by this hunk.

Reviewed exact CP2 frame lengths, echoed selector checks, status/metadata consistency and reply-length scanner used by USB/BLE parsing. Mismatched or malformed responses fail closed rather than updating the selected resource.

Reviewed CP1 mode acknowledgement, snapshot-pending retry after display idle, captured connection generation and runtime state dispatch. Existing applied-slot source remains authoritative; no slot-binding/TTL contract change found.

Reviewed connection generations, display admission and leases, uncertainty quarantine, legacy transaction ordering, response routing, disconnect reset, 0x00 status exception, deferred runtime state and USB/BLE transport pinning. Actual typed legacy callers that share commandTransactionLock serialize with display reads; controlled tests cover the identified orderings. No overlapping CP2/legacy response path found in reviewed call graph.

Reviewed import/migration, target snapshot, worker serialization, connection and operation checks, on-demand reads, dirty-value merge, preview/save ACK paths, partial nine-item saves, upload persistence and stale callback filtering. No P0/P1 issue found. A failed light-bar refresh conservatively marks OLED current device facts unknown too; local assets and historical metadata remain intact, so this is not treated as a blocking data-loss defect.
